config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification, using the five-part question pattern (1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks) that applies from summer 2026. Not past-paper material. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other valid answers are credited.

Beliefs.1: 1 mark. Either a multiple-choice question (choose the one correct option from A–D) or a short-response 'Give one…' question. One accurate, relevant answer earns the mark; no explanation is needed. AO1:1 knowledge.
Beliefs.4: 4 marks (AO1:2 influence). Typically 'Explain two ways in which belief in … influences Sikhs today.' For each way: simple explanation of a relevant and accurate influence = 1 mark; detailed (developed) explanation = 2 marks. Two ways × 2 marks.
Beliefs.6: 6 marks (AO1:1). 'Explain two Sikh teachings about … Refer to sacred writings or another source of Sikh belief and teaching in your answer.' Each teaching: simple explanation 1 mark, detailed explanation 2 marks (max 4). Source of authority: 2 marks for naming a relevant source AND applying it to the question; 1 mark for naming it only, or for applying it without naming it.
Beliefs.12: 12 marks (AO2) plus up to 3 SPaG marks. 'Evaluate this statement' – refer to Sikh teaching, give reasoned arguments for the statement and for a different view, reach a justified conclusion. Levels: L4 (10–12) well-argued, reasoned consideration of different views, logical chains of reasoning leading to judgements supported by relevant knowledge, religion applied to the issue; L3 (7–9) reasoned consideration of different views, logical chains of reasoning, clear reference to religion; L2 (4–6) reasoned consideration of one view, or recognition of different views each with reasons (max L2 with no reference to religion); L1 (1–3) a point of view with reason(s) stated.

Practices.1: 1 mark. Either a multiple-choice question (choose the one correct option from A–D) or a short-response 'Give one…' question. One accurate, relevant answer earns the mark; no explanation is needed. AO1:1 knowledge.
Practices.4: 4 marks (AO1:2/AO1:3). Typically 'Explain two different ways in which Sikhs …' or 'Explain two ways in which … influences Sikhs today.' For each way: simple explanation 1 mark; detailed explanation 2 marks. Where 'different' is asked, the two ways must genuinely differ.
Practices.6: 6 marks (AO1:1). 'Explain two … Refer to sacred writings or another source of Sikh belief and teaching in your answer.' Each point: simple explanation 1 mark, detailed explanation 2 marks (max 4). Source of authority: 2 marks for naming a relevant source AND applying it to the question; 1 mark for naming only, or applying without naming.
Practices.12: 12 marks (AO2) plus up to 3 SPaG marks. 'Evaluate this statement' – refer to Sikh teaching, give reasoned arguments for the statement and for a different view, reach a justified conclusion. Levels: L4 (10–12) well-argued, reasoned consideration of different views, logical chains of reasoning leading to judgements supported by relevant knowledge, religion applied to the issue; L3 (7–9) reasoned consideration of different views, logical chains, clear reference to religion; L2 (4–6) reasoned consideration of one view, or different views each with reasons (max L2 with no reference to religion); L1 (1–3) a point of view with reason(s) stated.
